documents.title: Required Sections: Artificial Intelligence Statements
tiers: Broader Use of Generative AI Permitted Within Guidelines
Use of Generative AI Permitted Under Some Circumstances or with Explicit Permission
No Use of Generative AI Permitted
documents.summary: A page of required syllabus sections includes three ready-made AI statements that faculty pick from, ranging from broad permitted use with citation to a full ban. NMSU sets the menu, and each instructor chooses.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Select one of the following three statements that best fits your course', offering tiers from permitted to no use, so the university sets no single stance and leaves the choice to instructors.

units.why: The page tells faculty to choose one of three statements, so the university sets the menu and each instructor decides per course. 'Select one' binds instructors; coded P04 because the point is who decides, not that a statement must exist (P09).
units.anchor: Select one of the following three statements that best fits your course to include.

units.why: Three named statements ranging from broad use to none are offered, which are explicit tiers of AI use (P05). 'AI Statements are now available for faculty to include in their syllabi' announces them.
units.anchor: AI Statements are now available for faculty to include in their syllabi.
units.policy: The university makes three AI statements available for faculty to include in their syllabi.
units.fit_note: Also covers that the statements are a syllabus-inclusion resource, not only the tier list.

units.why: The first tier says use is 'permitted ... for students who wish to use them', so AI is allowed by default in courses that choose it; P02, with conditions coded in the next units.
units.anchor: AI tools is permitted in this course for students who wish to use them.
units.frag_start: Use of AI tools is permitted

units.why: The first tier says students 'must cite' AI material that informed their work, in text and in references; this is disclosure with each submission (P24), not the tool/prompt detail of P25.
units.anchor: Students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work
units.policy: Students must cite any AI-generated material that informed their work, including in-text citations and/or use of quotations, and in the references list.

units.why: Generating content without attribution 'qualifies as academic dishonesty', so undisclosed AI use is classed as misconduct (P36). P28 (nondisclosure as the violation) also fits, but the misconduct classification is the main claim.
units.anchor: Using an AI tool to generate content without proper attribution qualifies as academic dishonesty.
units.frag_start: Using an AI tool to generate
units.fit_note: Also makes failure to attribute the violation (P28).

units.why: The second tier says students 'will be informed as to when, where, and how' AI tools are permitted, so permission is set assignment by assignment by the instructor (P04).
units.anchor: You will be informed as to when, where, and how these tools are permitted
units.frag_start: You will be informed as to
units.policy: Students are informed when, where, and how AI writing tools are permitted to be used, along with guidance for attribution.
units.fit_note: Also says the instructor supplies attribution guidance.

units.why: 'we may use AI Writing tools' grants conditional permission limited to occasions the instructor specifies, a restrictive default. No type fits this tier's default exactly, so P04 is closest and the note records the gap.
units.anchor: During this class, we may use AI Writing tools.
units.fit_note: The statement is limited to AI writing tools and allows use only when the instructor says so.

units.why: This tier says permitted tools 'should be used with caution and proper citation'. The citation part is disclosure (P24); the caution has no type, hence the fit_note.
units.anchor: they should be used with caution and proper citation
units.fit_note: Also advises using AI tools with caution, which no type captures.

units.why: The third tier assumes all submitted work is 'generated by the students themselves', so students own what they submit (P29) and the ban rests on that.
units.anchor: all work submitted by students will be generated by the students themselves
units.frag_start: This course assumes that all work
units.policy: The course assumes that all work submitted by students will be generated by the students themselves, working individually or in groups.

units.why: It says students should not have another person or entity write substantive parts of assignments, naming 'using AI tools'; AI may not produce submitted work (P19).
units.anchor: Students should not have another person/entity do the writing of any substantive portion
units.policy: Students should not have another person or entity do the writing of any substantive portion of an assignment for them, which includes hiring a person or a company to write assignments and using AI tools.

units.why: The third tier is titled 'No Use of Generative AI Permitted', a blanket course-level ban (P01).
units.anchor: No Use of Generative AI Permitted

documents.title: Inclusion of Syllabus language clearly stating the level of use of AI permitted in each course at NMSU
tiers: Broader Use of Generative AI Permitted Within Guidelines
Use of Generative AI Permitted Under Some Circumstances or with Explicit Permission
No Use of Generative AI Permitted
documents.summary: A January 2024 provost memo requires faculty to tell students the level of AI use allowed in each course and introduces three syllabus options. It also names benefits and concerns and promises training.
documents.stance_why: The memo requires clarity on 'the level of use of AI permitted in each course' but sets no AI stance itself, offering three options for faculty to choose from.

units.why: The memo says students 'must be informed' of acceptable AI use in each course, so instructors must state AI expectations (P09).
units.anchor: students must be informed as to the acceptable use, or otherwise, of AI
units.frag_start: students must be informed as to

units.why: The memo says clarity of expectations is needed while the landscape changes. It states the purpose of the syllabus requirement, an institution-level principle (P56).
units.anchor: we need to maintain a clarity of expectations for our students
units.frag_start: we need to maintain a clarity

units.why: The syllabus generator and Canvas template now offer three options for faculty, effective Spring 2024; P05 because they set levels of use.
units.anchor: three options for faculty to choose from that will inform the student
units.policy: The syllabus generator and Canvas template contain three options for faculty to choose from that inform the student what level of AI use the instructor will accept in the class, effective Spring 2024.
units.fit_note: Also records the effective date and the delivery channel (syllabus generator, Canvas template).

units.why: The memo lists the three named levels, saying they 'encompass all potential level of possible use'; P05 names tiers. P04 also touches instructor choice, but the named levels are the content.
units.anchor: Broader Use of Generative AI Permitted WithinGuidelines
units.frag_end: No Use of Generative AI Permitted.
units.policy: The three choices are Broader Use of Generative AI Permitted Within Guidelines; Use of Generative AI Permitted Under Some Circumstances or with Explicit Permission; No Use of Generative AI Permitted.

units.why: The memo says the syllabus generator 'always has the most up-to-date information', pointing faculty to a maintained source. Nearest type is P54, but it says the tool is kept current, not that the AI policy will be revisited.
units.anchor: The syllabus generator always has the most up-to-date information in all aspects
units.fit_note: Says the generator is kept up to date rather than that the AI policy will be revisited.

units.why: The language came from a fall 2023 task force with many stakeholders. This describes how and by whom the policy was made; no type covers provenance.
units.anchor: This language was the outcome from a fall 2023 AI task force
units.uncovered_note: Describes the task force and stakeholder process that produced the university's AI syllabus language.

units.why: The memo lists advantages of AI (personalization, efficiency, insights, accessibility) as balanced rationale. No type covers stated benefits of AI, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: enhanced personalization, efficiency and automation, data-driven insights, and increased accessibility and inclusivity
units.frag_start: The use of AI in education offers
units.policy: The use of AI in education offers numerous advantages, including enhanced personalization, efficiency and automation, data-driven insights, and increased accessibility and inclusivity.
units.uncovered_note: States general benefits of AI in education (personalization, efficiency, accessibility) as balanced rationale.

units.why: The memo names concerns: 'ethical considerations, dependency and over-reliance, equity and access'. P53 (ethical concerns) is primary; equity (P51) and detection (P39) are secondary.
units.anchor: ethical considerations, dependency and over-reliance, equity and access
units.frag_end: effective tools to detect AI content.
units.policy: Concerns about AI include ethical considerations, dependency and over-reliance, equity and access, and the current lack of effective tools to detect AI content.
units.fit_note: Also names equity and access (P51) and the lack of detection tools (P39).

units.why: Collaboration, mutual training and ethical reflection are urged for faculty ('we should seek training and support from each other'); this is faculty learning about AI (P63).
units.anchor: we should seek training and support from each other
units.frag_start: we should seek training and support
units.policy: Faculty should seek training and support from each other and consider the ethical implications of incorporating AI into teaching methodologies.

units.why: The memo promises campus training opportunities in spring for 'everyone who wishes to participate'. Faculty are the addressees, so P63; the open audience is noted.
units.anchor: There will be campus opportunities in the spring for everyone who wishes to participate
units.fit_note: Says 'everyone' may participate, not only faculty (P70).

notes: No school or computing-unit policies found; course layer deferred.
